# GEO report: ledger-site

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 72/100, Good

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.5 ÷ 23 × 100 = 72. High = (16.5 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 72.

This is a small Next.js App Router site. I sampled four routes: `/`, `/pricing`, `/docs` and `/blog`. The basics are in good shape. Four things cost points: `robots.txt` doesn't point to the sitemap, `<html>` has no `lang`, two pages have no canonical link, and two pages have their own problems (`/pricing` is `noindex`, and `/blog` is rendered only in the browser). Every rule could be settled from code, so nothing is unknown. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

**Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Point robots.txt at your sitemap
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers read `robots.txt` first, and it's the usual way they find your sitemap (your list of pages). Yours exists but isn't announced.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:1`
- **What the code says:** the file has only `User-agent: *`, `Allow: /`, `User-agent: GPTBot` and `Disallow: /`, with no `Sitemap:` line.
- **Size:** Small. Add `Sitemap: https://www.ledger.example/sitemap.xml`.
- **Score after this:** 80 (18.5 ÷ 23).

### 2. Set the page language and give /blog its own title and description
- **Why it matters:** The `lang` attribute tells machines what language the page is in. `/blog` also has no metadata of its own, so it shows the same title and description as the home page.
- **Where:** `app/layout.tsx:10` and `app/blog/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `<html>` with no `lang`. `/blog` uses `'use client'` and exports no `metadata`.
- **Size:** Small. Use `<html lang="en">`, which matches `site.language` in `geo.config.json`. For the `/blog` metadata, move the interactive part into a client component, so the page itself can export `metadata`.
- **Score after this:** 80 (18.5 ÷ 23).

### 3. Add canonical links to /docs and /blog
- **Why it matters:** A canonical link names the main address of a page. Without one, search engines have to guess between duplicate addresses.
- **Where:** `app/docs/page.tsx:1`
- **What the code says:** `export const metadata = { title: 'Docs', description: 'How to set up Ledger.' };` has no `alternates.canonical`. `/blog` has none either.
- **Size:** Small. Add `alternates: { canonical: 'https://www.ledger.example/docs' }`, and the same for `/blog`.
- **Score after this:** 76 (17.5 ÷ 23). The `/blog` canonical needs the metadata change from item 2, so doing items 2 and 3 together gives more than the sum of each alone.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Live | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt is valid and within size limits | Clear | Not run | `public/robots.txt` is valid plain text |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers get the access your policy says | Clear | Not run | `User-agent: *` / `Allow: /` at `public/robots.txt:1`. Only GPTBot (training) is blocked, which matches your policy. |
| GEO-014 | Listed and linked pages are indexable | Problem | Not run | `app/pricing/page.tsx:1` has `robots: { index: false, follow: true }`. It's in the sitemap and the nav. 3 of 4 routes are clear. |
| GEO-015 | One absolute canonical on your domain | Problem | Not run | `/` and `/pricing` are clear. `/docs` and `/blog` have none (2 of 4 clear). |
| GEO-003 | Content is in the server HTML | Problem | Not run | `app/blog/page.tsx:7` fetches posts in `useEffect`, so the server HTML has an empty list. The other 3 routes are clear. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD is valid | Not applicable | Not run | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap is valid and discoverable | Problem | Not run | The sitemap is valid, but `public/robots.txt` has no `Sitemap:` line. Site-wide. |
| GEO-012 | Title, description and `lang` | Problem | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:10` has `<html>` with no `lang`. Site-wide. `/blog` also inherits the home page's title and description. |
| GEO-016 | Key routes are reachable by normal links | Clear | Not run | `app/layout.tsx:11` has `<a href>` links in a server-rendered nav to all four routes |
| GEO-017 | Snippet limits don't conflict with AI search | Clear | Not run | Only element-level `data-nosnippet` at `app/layout.tsx:14`. No middleware or `headers()` found. |
| GEO-002 | Basic accessibility | Clear | Not run | I read `app/layout.tsx` and all five pages. There are no images or buttons, the links have text and every page has a title. |
| GEO-101 | Mobile app association files | Not applicable | Not run | No app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info only) | Not applicable | Not run | Not present. Optional and not scored. |

## Other problems found

- `public/sitemap.xml:4` lists `https://www.ledger.example/pricing`, but the page is `noindex` (`app/pricing/page.tsx:1`). Either remove `robots: { index: false, follow: true }` from `app/pricing/page.tsx` or drop the URL from the sitemap. This is the same issue as GEO-014. I'm repeating it because it sends mixed signals.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. If you have an access log, `geopilot logs <access log>` checks real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **Status codes and headers:** whether pages answer 200 and whether any `X-Robots-Tag` header is added outside the repo.
- **Server HTML for `/blog`:** a live check would confirm what crawlers receive.

## Assumptions

- You want search engines and AI search tools to find this site. This matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- I treated `/thank-you` as intentionally `noindex`. It isn't in the sitemap or the nav, so I didn't count it.
- I assumed that `/pricing` being `noindex` may be a mistake, since you link to it and list it in the sitemap. If it's deliberate, remove it from the sitemap and nav instead.
- The origin is `https://www.ledger.example`, from `geo.config.json`.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-014`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
